rationale: C21 supplies a particularly close reusable template: it opens specified tax returns to inspection by a special congressional committee established under a numbered resolution, states that inspection is for carrying out that resolution, and incorporates conditions in a contemporaneously approved Treasury decision. The child follows this same operative sequence and largely the same wording, while adapting the tax-return category, years, chamber, resolution, committee mandate, and expiration date. C03 and C25 use nearly identical machinery, but C21 is strongest because it also concerns a special committee and uses the same resolution-purpose formulation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: any return on Form 990—A ... shall ... be open to inspection by the special committee of the House of Representatives authorized by House Resolution 217
shared_material.parent_excerpt: any ... tax returns ... shall be open to inspection by the Special Committee established pursuant to Senate Resolution 202
shared_material.explanation: Both authorize inspection of defined tax returns by a special congressional committee created or authorized through a specific resolution.

shared_material.child_excerpt: for the purpose of carrying out the provisions of such resolution
shared_material.parent_excerpt: for the purpose of carrying out the provisions of the said Senate Resolution
shared_material.explanation: This is a close, distinctive verbal match linking the inspection authority directly to the committee resolution.

shared_material.child_excerpt: subject to the conditions stated in the Treasury decision ... relating to the inspection of returns by certain committees of the Congress, approved by me this date
shared_material.parent_excerpt: subject to the conditions stated in the Treasury decision relating to the inspection of such returns by that Committee, approved by me this date
shared_material.explanation: The same administrative mechanism subjects inspection to a Treasury decision approved contemporaneously.
